title: The Quran: Surah 113, al-Falaq (Daybreak)
author: Tradução inglesa de Talal Itani (ClearQuran)
tradition: Texto sagrado do Islão, século VII
intro: Lição sobre a Surata 113. O texto inglês é a tradução de Talal Itani, reproduzida sem alterações; as notas de língua, perguntas, discussão e escrita são material pedagógico separado, baseado apenas no que o próprio texto diz.

source.title: Quran English Translation: Clear, Pure, Easy to Read Modern English
source.edition: Edition A (uses the word 'Allah' to refer to the Creator)

questions.q: With whom does the speaker take refuge, according to verse 1?
options: The Lord of the two Easts
questions.why: O versículo 1 diz: 'I take refuge with the Lord of Daybreak.'
'Take refuge' é procurar abrigo ou protecção.

questions.q: Verse 3 says 'the darkness as it gathers'. What time of day does this suggest?
options: The evening, when night is coming
It suggests no time at all
questions.why: 'As it gathers' mostra a escuridão a aumentar, e contrasta com 'Daybreak' do versículo 1.

options: Each names something from whose evil the speaker asks protection
questions.why: Cada versículo tem 'the evil of' seguido de algo: o que Ele criou, a escuridão, os que praticam feitiçaria, um invejoso.

questions.q: Which one is NOT mentioned in the passage?
questions.why: O texto menciona a escuridão, a feitiçaria e a inveja; não menciona a fome.

B2.discussion: The speaker asks for protection from several things. What do people usually ask protection from today? Give examples.
B2.writing: Write 80 to 100 words: Say what the speaker asks for and what he asks protection from.

questions.q: What does the darkness do in verse 3?
questions.why: O versículo 3 diz 'the darkness as it gathers'.

questions.q: In 'an envious when he envies', 'envious' is used as:
options: an adjective used to name a person
questions.why: 'An envious' refere-se a uma pessoa, e 'he envies' usa o verbo correspondente.

questions.q: What contrast do verse 1 and verse 3 create?
options: Between Daybreak and darkness as it gathers
questions.why: O versículo 1 fala do romper do dia e o versículo 3 da escuridão a reunir-se.

questions.q: What phrase is repeated in verses 2 to 5?
questions.why: 'The evil of' aparece em todos os versículos de 2 a 5 e organiza a lista.

questions.q: 'The evil of an envious when he envies.' What does 'when he envies' add?
options: It ties the danger to the moment the envy is at work
It says he envies only once
It says he lives far away
questions.why: 'When he envies' liga o mal ao momento em que a inveja actua.

C1.discussion: The passage moves from something very general ('what He created') to specific dangers. What does this order suggest about how the speaker organises the request?
C1.writing: Write 120 to 150 words: Explain how the repetition in verses 2 to 5 shapes the passage.

questions.q: Which is the first general danger named after verse 1?
options: The evil of what He created
questions.why: O versículo 2 é o primeiro: 'From the evil of what He created.'
A expressão é muito ampla e os versículos seguintes concretizam-na.

questions.q: How do verses 3 to 5 relate to verse 2?
options: They give specific cases after a general statement
questions.why: O versículo 2 é geral; os versículos 3, 4 e 5 nomeiam casos concretos: escuridão, feitiçaria e inveja.

questions.q: The repetition of 'the evil of' at the start of each item is an example of:
options: a repeated opening that gives the passage a steady rhythm
questions.why: A repetição no início de cada item cria um ritmo regular e organiza a lista.

questions.q: Which reading is best supported by the passage?
options: It names a shelter and then lists several dangers, moving from broad to specific
It tells the story of a single event
questions.why: O versículo 1 diz onde procurar refúgio; os versículos 2 a 5 percorrem os perigos, do geral ao concreto.

C2.discussion: Daybreak and the gathering darkness appear at opposite ends of the opening verses. What effect does this contrast have on how the reader hears the request for refuge?
C2.writing: Write 150 to 200 words: Analyse how the structure of verses 1 to 5 moves from shelter to danger, referring to specific words.
